correctness.rationale: For fixed zero vertex set Z avoiding positive-edge endpoints, zero-target surviving edges force one projective direction; positive-target edges force different directions. Contracting zero edges in a forest preserves foresthood and leaves r edges and c(U) components, giving (q+1)^c q^r direction choices. Positive-edge multiplicative scalar constraints are independent across the forest, leaving (q-1)^(|U|-r) scalar choices. Summation and two free central coordinates give the exact count. Direct complete finite enumeration passes 101 graph-field configurations; proof covers all q, including characteristic two.
